[Yāska:] '*Atiṣṭhantīnām aniviśamānānām*, that is, of the non-stationary — in the midst of the waters (*kāṣṭhānām*) is placed the body, the cloud. *Śarīra* from *śṝ* or from *śam*. *Vṛtrasya niṇyam*: the nameless [body] of Vṛtra the waters move over (*vicaranti*), i.e. know (*vijānanti*). *Dīrgham* from *drāgh*, *tamas* from *tan*, *āśayat* from *ā-śī*. *Indraśatruḥ*: Indra is its pacifier or its destroyer, hence *indraśatruḥ*. Who then is Vṛtra? The cloud, say the etymologists; the *asura*, son of Tvaṣṭṛ, say the historians' (Ni. 2. 16). [End of Varga 37.] *(Mine, tentative.)*
